scope: Isolated Home Assistant instance; no live installation or notifications.
Refresh: 6002 entities; three samples per state-change case.
Save: 6000 entities and 300 devices; real runtime Store write/readback with temporary filesystem storage; registries mocked; notifications disabled.
Probes serialized on this worker; wall-clock values are host-dependent observations, not performance guarantees.
measurements.timing_disclaimer: Phase timings are inclusive and overlap: engine_policy includes discovery when present; persistence includes snapshot_creation and durable verification. Do not sum phase timings. Before/after timings vary; deterministic work counts are the primary regression guard.

panel_payload.note: New opt-in panel payload is reported separately; legacy subscribers retain their existing summary. Refresh measure dashboard_bytes counts the legacy update and is not the panel payload size.

remaining_cost: Selected temperature observations still evaluate and durably save once; eliminating discovery does not eliminate snapshot creation, disk write, and verification.
Policy parameter changes still rediscover and reconcile monitoring; this retained repeat is slower than baseline and no threshold-save speedup is claimed.
Notification saves still drain ordered queued observations while holding the runtime mutation lock. Fifty queued transitions dominate burst-save latency.
Runtime persistence snapshots remain approximately 14.5 to 15.4 MB in these fixtures; no persistence or outbox durability reduction was made.
